description: Stores chemical and isotopic analytical results for samples, including major and trace element concentrations, isotope ratios, laboratory references, analytical setup links, and bibliographic references documenting each analysis.
Stores sample records, linking each sample to its site, typological classification, sampling manager, metallurgy type, bibliographic references, and free-text comments.
Reference table for chemical elements, including atomic number, IUPAC chemical symbol, element name, atomic weight, density, melting temperature, and boiling temperature.
Stores calculated measurement errors associated with analyses, with one error value per measured chemical element and a foreign key linking each error record to its corresponding analysis.
Stores hierarchical geographic and administrative location names, from country through administrative subdivisions to locality, including the administrative type at each level.
Stores analytical uncertainty values by instrument, element, and concentration interval, defining the uncertainty applicable within each minimum and maximum measurement range.
Stores limits of detection for chemical elements measured by analytical devices, linking each detection limit value to an instrument and element.
Stores bibliographic references used in the database, including authors, title, journal or book, volume, issue, publication year, pages, URL, DOI, and publication type.
Stores metadata about analytical devices and methods, including laboratory, analytical method, instrument manufacturer, and model.
Stores information about people involved in the project, including first name, last name, affiliated organization, and email address.

Stores archaeological, geographic, or sampling context information, including locality links, context name, spatial coordinates, coordinate reference system, date range, uncertainty flag, PeriodO keys, EDTF date, and site name.
Reference table for spatial reference systems, including SRID identifiers, authority names and codes, WKT metadata, and PROJ.4 transformation definitions.
Stores typological classifications for samples in French and English, covering metallurgical process, context, material, category, sub-category, and external ARK reference.
